tasks.title: Circumpolar stars
tasks.statement:
Circumpolar stars. Usually we consider that there are about 6000 stars in the whole sky which are visible to the naked eye. The refraction near the horizon is 35'. Find, how many more stars visible to the naked eye become circumpolar (which means that they never set) due to refraction:
In your solution include a picture with an image of the Bear on the ices of North Pole and the Giraffe on the Equator, and necessary dimensions and/or angular dimensions used.

parts.question: for observer on the North Pole at zero height position (like Polar Bear in a position with its eyes at zero height).
for observer on the Equator at zero height position (like Giraffe with the eyes lowered to zero level).

tasks.title: Observation of a star
tasks.statement: Observation of a star. A star is observed from the Earth. It is found that its magnitude is m1 = 2.74 when observed at Zenith and m2 = 2.85 when observed at 45° above the horizon. What would the apparent magnitude m0 of the star be if observed from above the atmosphere (from a satellite, for example)?

parts.question: What would the apparent magnitude m0 of the star be if observed from above the atmosphere?

tasks.title: Parallax
tasks.statement: Parallax. Like humans, astronomers of Mercury use the same method for definitions of parallaxes and of parsec but measure them in different (their own) units. For example, the distance to Sirius equals to 1.406 mepc (1.406 mercurial parsec).

parts.question: Describe the most evident system of angular units used by astronomers of Mercury.
parts.reference: Решение и критерии для первого вопроса задачи 3.

parts.question: Calculate the mercurial diurnal parallax of the Sun and write the answer in "meau" (mercurial angular units - the common angular units for astronomers of Mercury).
parts.reference: Решение и критерии для второго вопроса задачи 3.

tasks.title: Climate
tasks.statement: Climate. There is a reference to climate in Crimea according to observations during 934 months between 1821 and 1991 on the web-site of the XV IAO. The average temperatures in Simferopol in January and July are equal to -0.4° C and +21.2° C respectively according to that data. Imagine a planet whose axis of rotation is perpendicular to the planets' ecliptic. Estimate, what the eccentricity of the planets' orbit should be in order to give climatic seasons identical to the ones in Crimea.

parts.question: Estimate, what the eccentricity of the planets' orbit should be in order to give climatic seasons identical to the ones in Crimea.

tasks.title: Cosmonaut
tasks.statement: Cosmonaut. Imagine a small space station with a total mass of M = 50 ton placed far away from any celestial body. A cosmonaut with a total mass (with ammunitions) of m = 100 kg appears L = 80 m away from the station without any fuel. Calculate (estimate) the time τ after which the cosmonaut reaches the station due to gravitational attraction. Consider the initial velocity of the cosmonaut to be zero.

parts.question: Calculate (estimate) the time τ after which the cosmonaut reaches the station due to gravitational attraction.
